newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO ministers submit resignation to Arafat.
newsitem.headline: PLO ministers submit resignation to Arafat.

text.p: All but two ministers in Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's 18-member cabinet offered to resign on Friday, a member of the cabinet said.

The move came a day after the Palestinian Legislative Council called on Arafat to dissolve his cabinet over alleged corruption and mismanagement and after Israel demanded he crack down on militants following a double suicide bombing in Jerusalem.

"Sixteen ministers submitted their resignation, except Yasser Abed Rabbo, of those who attended the meeting, and Nabil Shaath, who did not attend," Agriculture Minister Abdel Jawad Saleh told Reuters.
Another minister who refused to be identified said Arafat would decide at a later date whether or not to accept the resignations. "President Arafat did not comment," Saleh said.
The resignations came during a four-hour meeting of the Palestinian cabinet in the West Bank town of Ramallah.
The second minister said the resignations were intended to allow Arafat room to make reforms and were not related to the legislative council vote.
"We placed our resignations at the disposal of President Arafat in order to find a way to make reforms. It is not in response to demands of the council or external pressures," the minister said.
"It is just a way to deal with problems since we take the issues seriously."
The minister said Information Minister Abed Rabbo refused to sign a resignation paper.

Minister of Planning and International Cooperation Shaath, also a senior PLO negotiator with Israel, was named in a legislative council report as one minister suspected of financial wrongdoing. Shaath has denied the allegations.
